verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Trigger.dev is a TypeScript-first platform: workflows are authored through a single `@trigger.dev/sdk` module, and it is positioned for 'TypeScript teams'. Python appears only 'via build extension', which is a build-system hook rather than a native Python workflow-authoring SDK. There is no evidence of Go or other language SDKs, nor of any feature parity across SDKs, so the multi-language story is not delivered.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I author workflows in the language my team already uses — TypeScript, Python, Go, or more — with real feature parity across SDKs

citations.quote: Language | TypeScript/JavaScript (Node.js and Bun); Python via build extension
All `v3` functionality is provided through the `@trigger.dev/sdk` module.
Choose Trigger.dev for TypeScript teams building production background jobs and AI agents in their codebase.
